title: Speaking Part 1 — the interview
note: One voice per topic, not three. The old file carried a Simple/Natural/Advanced register alongside each dialogue; Advanced read like a written paragraph rather than something a candidate would say, and the register index was quietly being reused as if it were the same thing as Build's school/university/working life-stage selector, which it isn't. Dropping the register axis removes both problems at once: there is nothing here to mislabel, and nothing here for the life-stage selector to be confused with. Build still offers three lives; Listen and Read show one candidate's answer per question, the way the exam actually sounds.

dialogue.t: What do you usually do at the weekend?
Oh, I love weekends. I usually meet up with my friends, because during the week we hardly get the chance to see each other properly.
Do you prefer Saturdays or Sundays?
Saturdays, definitely. To be honest, Sundays are a bit ruined by homework, because I always end up spending most of the afternoon catching up on schoolwork before Monday.
Is there anything you'd like to do at weekends but don't have time for?
Yes, actually. I'd love to learn to skate properly, but there's never quite enough time, so it keeps getting pushed to some vague point in the future.
Do you live in a house or a flat?
Well, I live in a flat in the city centre. Actually, I've been living there for about three years now.
Can you describe the place where you live?
To be honest, it's quite spacious for a city flat. It has two bedrooms, a modern kitchen, and a lovely balcony overlooking the park. What I really like is that it gets a lot of natural light.

dialogue.t: How long have you lived there?
As I mentioned, I've been there for about three years. I moved in right after I started my current job, so it's been my home for quite a while now.
Where are you from?
I'm originally from a small coastal town in the south of Portugal. It's called Lagos. It's quite a picturesque place with beautiful beaches.
What do you like about your hometown?
Well, I absolutely love the relaxed atmosphere. People are very friendly and welcoming. Plus, the weather is amazing – we have sunshine almost year-round.
What do you not like about it?
To be frank, the main downside is the lack of job opportunities. It's very tourism-dependent, so career options are quite limited. That's actually why I moved to the city.
Do you work or are you a student?
I'm currently working. I've been in the same company for the past two years now.
What do you do?
I work as a marketing coordinator for a tech startup. Basically, I handle social media campaigns, content creation, and analyse customer engagement data.
Why did you choose that job?

Well, I've always been interested in digital marketing and technology. The company offered me a great opportunity to combine both interests. On top of that, the startup environment is fast-paced and innovative, which I find really exciting.
What do you like doing in your free time?
Well, I'm really into photography. I love going out with my camera and capturing interesting moments. I also enjoy reading, especially historical fiction.
How much time do you have to relax?
To be frank, not as much as I'd like. During the week, I'm quite busy with work, so I only have a couple of hours in the evening. However, weekends are when I can really unwind.
How do you usually relax?
I'd say my go-to way to relax is going for a walk in nature. It helps me clear my mind. Alternatively, I like watching documentaries or listening to podcasts while doing some light stretching.
Do you like travelling?
Absolutely! I'm passionate about travelling. I find it incredibly enriching to experience different cultures and meet new people. It really broadens your perspective.
How often do you travel?
Well, I try to travel at least twice a year. Usually, I take one longer trip during the summer and a shorter city break in winter. Of course, it depends on my work schedule and budget.
Where did you go on your last trip?

My last trip was to Barcelona. I went there last autumn for a long weekend. I was blown away by the architecture, especially Gaudí's work. The food was also fantastic – I tried so many delicious tapas!
